 Trending How to watch: Washington State vs. Boise State 
 Washington State vs. Boise State: 5 Keys with CouGreat Mkristo Bruce
 Cougars have to control time of possession and take Boise State out of a rhythm
 Jamey Vinnick 0 PULLMAN --  Let Owen Eshelman go to work. Coming into a game with a 1-6 record, Washington State has very little to lose vs. Boise State. So let the second-year quarterback continue to roll after an impressive debut, says CouGreat defensive end Mkristo Bruce . 
 The Cougars are heavy underdogs vs. Boise State but the slow, deliberate offense of the Broncos offers a better opportunity than the high-octane explosiveness of Oregon State, whom the Cougars struggled to slow down last week.
 Here are Bruce's five keys for the Cougars to get conference win No. 1 in the Kirby Moore era.
 1. SUSTAIN DRIVES AND DON'T LET BOISE STATE MANAGE THE CLOCK THE WAY IT WANTS 
 Boise State wins games with a steady rushing attack and by controlling the ball. The Broncos lead the country in time of possession, keeping the ball for a whopping 36:41 per game. WSU is 101st at 28:43.
 The Cougars have struggled mightily at sustaining possessions and that has often led to opponents wearing the defense down toward the end of games. The offense was more potent last week and that could make a difference. But in some ways, the 15-play, 83-yard touchdown drive may work better for the Cougars than the one explosive play.
 Bruce's thoughts:  "Scoring is great. But we haven't proven that we can do that. Priority is points by any means necessary. But we can't live on quick possessions either. And three-and-outs have been the Achilles' heel this year for Wazzu. 
 "Move the chains, convert on third down, and keep our defense off the field. The longer our offense stays out there, the less time Boise State has to pound the football and control the clock. We have talent in the backfield and there has to be more packages to get the ball in Maxwell Woods' hands. This may mean getting him in the slot and finding holes to sit down in to get in open space." 
 2. LET ESHELMAN COOK 
 The path to a WSU victory almost certainly depends on Eshelman. He was excellent at Oregon State, but there was also no tape on him. Boise State will have more to go off of and try and slow him down, but the player we saw last week has explosive capabilities.
 There are going to be growing pains with a young quarterback. But even if Boise State does certain things to try and limit him, don't put the training wheels back on. Let Eshelman do what he can do even if that means some bumps in the road.
 Bruce's thoughts: "We saw what this kid is capable of. Now take the training wheels off even more and let him cook. Even as a young QB, he looks comfortable in the pocket so Kirby Moore can open up the playbook. Let him use his legs, push the ball downfield and make plays. He's going to make some mistakes, but that's part of growing. You can't play scared. Let Owen be Owen, and let's see what the kid can do." 
 3. UTILIZE ZONE READS AND ESHELMAN'S LEGS TO OPEN UP THE GROUND GAME 
 One of the big surprises from last week was Eshelman rumbling 15 times for 136 yards and a touchdown. We knew he was mobile, but not necessarily to that degree. And while Boise State may be more prepared for that than Oregon State was, it may open up the rushing attack as a whole.
 Eshelman found a ton of success on read options and zone reads, and forcing Boise State to stay honest on Eshelman's threat to run may finally allow the running backs to find some room to run, room that has been largely absent through the first seven games.
 Bruce's thoughts:  "Owen's athleticism and decision making will be put to the test against this defensive front. We will need to find ways to slow them down to keep them honest. 
 "I also feel like Wazzu isn't putting any type of fear into the hearts of Boise State with the current run game. This is all a set up when you force that backside defender to respect the QB run. It creates running lanes for our backs and makes the defense defend all 11 guys. Caden Pinnick didn't really establish this, so having Eshelman's mentality of taking the easy yards or what the defense gives you is going to be key." 
 Related: Eshelman-Ganashamoorthy connection, Kirby Moore highlights Cougars' emerging playmakers 
 4. GET BOISE BEHIND THE STICKS 
 The Broncos aren't shy about their identity. They want to run and run and run. Keep the ball moving on first and second down, because it sets up easy opportunities to run on third down. 
 Maddux Madsen is a better quarterback than he gets credit for, but the path to victory is to make him throw the ball. If the Cougars can get the Broncos in third-and-long, it forces Madsen to beat them. And while he may still be able to do that, you will take your chances with him over RBs Dylan Riley and Sire Gaines.
 Bruce's thoughts:  "Boise State is dangerous when they can run the football and they can easily put up 200 yards on the ground and control the clock. We've got to win on first and second down. Create these third-and-long scenarios and force them into the passing game. If we allow for them to get four or five yards a pop on the ground it will be a recipe for a long day. Make them one-dimensional and put the pressure on Madsen to beat us through the air." 
 5. GET PRESSURE ON MADSEN, EVEN IF THAT MEANS FINALLY DRAWING HOLDING CALLS 
 WSU's pass rush has fallen flat the last two games, partly because of Utah State's quick pass game, partly because of Oregon State's explosive offense and dependent offensive line, and partly because the Cougars can't draw a holding call to save their lives.
 The WSU pass rushers need to get after the quarterback and if they can't, they need to do a better job of disengaging from blocks and drawing the flags. In some ways, getting the holding call can be more disruptive than even a sack. Make some sort of noise with the rush.
 Bruce's thoughts:  "This is a tough one because we have seen some good schemes on doing the best we can to keep games in reach on defense, even to the point where we are getting turnovers and scoring on defense. Hardest part is we need to blitz and we need to take some risks. But doing that and being down can be a huge gamble and expose ourselves to big gains. 
 "Kaden Beatty has to be a monster in the middle and allow Linus Zunk and Matyus McLain a chance to win on the edges. Lastly, I like the idea of Keith Brown blitzing the inside gaps to apply pressure and get tackles for loss." 
 Related: Q&A with OSU expert Jackson Naugle 
 WSU-BOISE STATE GAME DETAILS: 
 WHERE:  Martin Stadium
 KICKOFF:  Saturday, 3 p.m. Pacific
 TV: USA Network Nate Gatter, Ryan Leaf , Lauren Green
 RADIO:  Washington State IMG Radio Network 
 WEATHER FORECAST:  54 degrees, cloudy, light winds
 RECORDS:  WSU 1-6, Boise State is 5-1
 THE SERIES:  WSU leads 5-2
 ESPN matchup predictor:  8.3 percent chance WSU wins
 RANKINGS:  The Broncos are the No. 21 team in the country
 THE LINE:  Boise State by 13.5
 CF.C PREDICTION:  Boise State 38-23
 THE COACHES:  Moore is 1-6, Spencer Danielson is 29-9
 Mkristo Bruce cheering from the sidelines (Photo: Whittney Thornton/Cougfan.com) Mkristo Bruce , one of the most prolific sack masters in WSU history, capped his college career by being named first-team All-Pac-10 and second-team AP and Walter Camp All-American. The one-time quarterback from Renton started 34 consecutive games at defensive end for WSU.
